pathway.title: Fmc Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Earnings no longer carry the debt, and the damage is wider than one quarter's charges. Third-quarter 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was negative USD 558.6 million, and even before the pricing charges it would have been USD 113.0 million against USD 236.1 million a year earlier, a fall of 52.1%. Revenue excluding India and before the charges fell 16.2% over nine months, and gross margin was 10.81% of revenue against 35.73%. Price pressure on legacy products and lower volumes sit under the channel charges, so the earnings base to which leverage returns is lower than the FY2025 figure of USD 842.7 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2-9; calculation C2-10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54

Revenue durability is weak because the main franchise has lost patent protection and demand is being destocked. The two diamide product families supplied about 34.6% of FY2025 revenue, their composition-of-matter patents have expired in the major markets, and the company names generic producers, particularly in China, as a continuing pricing threat. Brazil and the United States supplied 58.8% of FY2025 revenue, customers are running very low inventory in response to high financing costs and demand uncertainty, and growers are buying carefully because of low crop prices and elevated input costs, so a regional destocking cycle reaches group earnings directly. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49

Liquidity is adequate for the next year but was bought with funding that does not repeat. Cash of USD 735.8 million and revolver availability of USD 1,661.4 million total USD 2,397.2 million, equal to 3.89 times the first-quarter 2026 operating cash outflow of USD 616.6 million, or 3.10 times if the USD 486.1 million of cash held by foreign subsidiaries is excluded. Net debt was USD 3,441.9 million at 2026-09-30 and USD 3,454.5 million pro forma for the USD 12.6 million dividend paid on 2026-10-15; pro forma cash and pro forma net leverage are not established. Only USD 72.8 million of principal falls due within one year and the revolver matures in 2028, so the near-term risk is cash burn and the covenant package, not a maturity. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2-1; calculation C2-2; calculation C2-3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69

Free cash flow has almost no room even on the pre-charge earnings base. Interest, dividends, guided environmental and restructuring spending and capital expenditure total USD 606.2 million to USD 636.2 million in 2026, against pre-charge last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 618.1 million, before cash taxes and working capital. The company expects 2026 free cash flow to be slightly below FY2025's negative USD 165.3 million, which caps fourth-quarter 2026 free cash flow at USD 123.6 million against USD 623.2 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, and nine-month free cash flow was negative USD 488.9 million without the Corteva prepayment. Basis: calculation C2-4; calculation C2-5; calculation C2-19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 78–79

The leverage test that returns on 2026-12-31 is the sharpest near-term risk and cannot be sized. The revolver covenant tests debt to adjusted earnings, not applied in the first three quarters of 2026, at a maximum of 6.75x through 2027-12-31, stepping down to 3.75x by the quarter ended March 31, 2029; interest cover must stay at 2.00x or more until June 30, 2027, rising to 3.50x by March 31, 2029. The company reports interest cover of 2.28x and secured leverage of 1.37x against a 3.50x maximum, yet its own Adjusted EBITDA over cash interest is negative 0.21x, so the covenant earnings definition must add back most of the third-quarter charges and the filings do not print it. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2-8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24

Structure now favours lien holders, and holders with no stated security are the exposed group. The USD 1,200.0 million of 8.00% senior secured notes due 2031 carry first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the company and its main guarantors, and the revolver is secured over certain assets, so secured debt is 32.0% of principal and could reach 51.2% if the available revolver were drawn. The filings state no security for the USD 2,000.0 million of senior notes or the USD 750.0 million of subordinated notes, so those holders rank behind the collateral on the same assets, and the December 2025 amendment also provided for a lien over substantially all assets if two agencies rate the company below BB+ or Ba1, a trigger whose status the filings do not state. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2-14; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24

Financial policy is supportive, but the equity cushion is thin and asset sales are conditional. The dividend was cut to USD 0.08 per share, repurchases are barred until 2028-12-31, and USD 603.2 million of equity and licence cash has been raised, with USD 366 million gross more pending from the India and Newark sales. Book equity is USD 9.5 million; at Tessenderlo's USD 13.30 purchase price, equity is worth USD 2,068.9 million, so debt is 66.9% of debt plus equity at that price, and the issuer estimates debt fair value at 90.4% of carrying value. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2-11; calculation C2-12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

Refinancing risk is about price and priority, not near-term dates. Of USD 4,222.8 million of principal, 82.9% matures after 2029, and the two newest series carry coupons of 8.00% and 8.45%, while third-quarter interest expense rose 14.82% on the prior year. A holder of the 2029 senior notes of USD 500.0 million faces the first large maturity after the revolver, and the secured structure is likely to make refinancing harder for holders with no stated security. Basis: calculation C2-6; calculation C2-13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

Claims outside debt are large relative to cash and compete with debt service. Accrued customer rebates of USD 811.9 million exceed cash at 2026-09-30 by USD 76.1 million (pro forma cash for the October dividend is not established), environmental liabilities are USD 566.0 million with about USD 304 million more reasonably possible, and the Corteva prepayment of USD 200.0 million is owed in product. None of these is in the USD 4,177.7 million of debt. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69

USD 3,467.4 million, down 18.3% from USD 4,246.1 million in FY2024; includes about USD 422 million of one-time revenue charges to prepare the India commercial business for sale
Insecticides 45.4%, herbicides 36.0%, fungicides 10.5%, plant health 5.5%, other 2.7% of revenue (rounded)
Latin America 39.0%, North America 31.8%, Europe, Middle East and Africa 25.1%, Asia 4.1%; Brazil (32.2%) and the United States (26.6%) each exceed 10% of revenue

Own sales organisations selling through distributors, retailers and co-operatives in four regions, plus direct sales to large growers in selected countries such as Brazil

Owned active-ingredient plants in the United States (Mobile), Puerto Rico (Manati), China (Jinshan), Denmark (Ronland) and India (Panoli), plus contract manufacturers; critical intermediates are sourced largely outside the United States, principally in China and India

Strengthen the balance sheet through asset sales and licensing, improve core portfolio competitiveness, manage the post-patent Rynaxypyr transition and support new actives (management language)

Revenue USD 105.9 million against USD 542.2 million a year earlier, after about USD 672 million of pricing and rebate charges, of which USD 639 million reduced revenue; gross margin negative USD 401.6 million

runs.text: The main credit strength is liquidity and funding access in the near term: USD 2,397.2 million of cash and revolver availability, a revolver that runs to 2028, only USD 72.8 million of principal due within one year, and no maturity above USD 150.0 million before the USD 500.0 million senior notes in 2029. The mechanism is that equity, a licence prepayment and secured notes retired the 2026 maturity and repaid the revolver, which gives creditors time. The implication is that a payment default before 2028 would likely need a cash burn well above the 2026 pattern.

A second strength is cooperative financial policy. The dividend is down to USD 0.08 per share, repurchases are barred until 2028-12-31, new equity went to debt repayment, and capital expenditure was cut 57.8% over nine months. The implication is that cash is being kept for creditors; cash dividends paid fell by USD 188.0 million in nine months 2026, which is modest next to cash interest of USD 250.8 million over twelve months.

A third strength is cost action and optionality: Project Foundation targets USD 200 million of annual run-rate savings by the end of 2027 and the pipeline includes four new active ingredients, and pending sales add USD 366 million gross. These are conditional and arrive after cash costs, so they support the downside case only if delivered.

The main weakness is the earnings collapse. Third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA was negative USD 558.6 million, the last twelve months are negative USD 53.5 million, and even pre-charge earnings fell 52.1% in the quarter. The mechanism is generic competition on the diamides and destocking by customers who face low crop prices, and the implication is that leverage cannot be sized and covenants, not earnings, set the pace.

The second weakness is priority and structure: first-lien secured notes and a secured revolver put 32.0% of principal ahead of the holders of senior and subordinated notes, for which no security is stated, rising to 51.2% on a full revolver draw, with a rating-triggered lien provision and repeated amendments that release and add collateral. The third is thin capital: total equity of USD 9.5 million, claims outside debt in the form of rebates of USD 811.9 million, environmental liabilities of USD 566.0 million and supplier finance of USD 213.1 million, and free cash flow near zero after fixed cash claims. The fourth is concentration, in one patent-exposed franchise and in Brazil and the United States.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Three transactions in 2026 repaired liquidity and two sales remain open. Tessenderlo Group bought 30,319,166 shares issued from treasury at USD 13.30 each, for cash proceeds of USD 403.2 million after announcing the agreement on 2026-06-30; the company paid USD 8.0 million of fees, used the proceeds to repay revolver borrowings and for general purposes, and called the investment the conclusion of the strategic review begun in February 2026. In June 2026 Corteva prepaid USD 200.0 million for rimisoxafen to be supplied by FMC under a co-exclusive supply and licence agreement, which the company records as deferred revenue and so as an obligation to deliver product. Basis: calculation C1A-2; calculation C1A-3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fmc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45

The new debt is USD 1,200.0 million of senior secured notes due 2031, completed on 2026-06-05 and used to redeem USD 500 million of senior notes due 2026-10-01, repay revolver borrowings and meet general corporate needs. The notes are guaranteed by subsidiaries in the United States, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Canada and Singapore and secured by first-priority liens, and the covenants on the notes limit dividends and further indebtedness. The revolver was amended in December 2025, April 2026, June 2026 and, after the balance sheet date, on 2026-10-21, each time changing covenant levels, security or the use of sale proceeds. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 45

Two sales remain open. The India commercial business is agreed for USD 252 million with Crystal Crop Protection Limited, subject to regulatory approvals and adjustments for cash, debt and working capital, with closing expected in 2026; its carrying value is USD 260.0 million, USD 8.0 million above the stated consideration before adjustments. The framework agreement for the Newark property, about USD 114 million gross with a leaseback, was expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 but the latest report says only that it is subject to due diligence. Events after 2026-09-30 are a dividend of USD 12.6 million paid on 2026-10-15 and the eighth revolver amendment, which requires net India proceeds to repay revolver debt or fund general or working capital needs and conditionally releases some guarantors and security; the dividend payment is not in September cash and the amendment is not in the terms reported at that date. Basis: calculation C1A-12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fmc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fmc Corp (FMC Corporation, issuer id fmc-37785), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the financial foundation: normalised statements, net debt, leverage, interest cover, liquidity, maturities and debt structure from the five supplied filings. No figure after 2026-10-30 is used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings no longer carry the debt: last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA was negative USD 53.5 million at 2026-09-30, so leverage cannot be measured and creditors depend on liquidity, covenant relief and pending asset sales. On adjusted EBITDA, total debt over EBITDA rose from 3.73x at FY2024 to 5.78x at 2026-06-30 before the third-quarter loss, and reported EBITDA is negative in every period after FY2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C-LA5; calculation C-LA4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was USD 3,441.9 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 3,490.4 million at 2025-12-31, held down by USD 403.2 million of equity proceeds and a USD 200.0 million licensing prepayment rather than by operations, whose cash flow was negative USD 285.5 million for nine months. Liquidity reached USD 2,397.2 million, and the interest coverage covenant passed at 2.28x against a 2.00x minimum on a definition the filings do not print.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C-N5; calculation C-O1; calculation C-LQ5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage worsened and then became unmeasurable because the earnings base collapsed, not because debt grew. Total debt over adjusted EBITDA was 3.73x at FY2024, 4.84x at FY2025, 5.70x at 2026-03-31 and 5.78x at 2026-06-30, while total debt at carrying value was USD 3,365.3 million, USD 4,074.9 million, USD 4,533.6 million and USD 4,280.6 million, and USD 4,177.7 million at 2026-09-30. At 2026-09-30 last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA is negative USD 53.5 million because the third quarter alone was negative USD 558.6 million, so neither the adjusted nor the reported ratio can be stated. For creditors this means the debt can no longer be sized against earnings: what decides whether leverage returns to a measurable range is the recovery of earnings, and the negative third quarter stays in the last-twelve-months figure until the third-quarter 2027 report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C-LA5; calculation C-Q5; calculation C-G5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 51

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage deteriorated in step with it: adjusted EBITDA over cash interest was 3.89x at FY2024, 3.55x at FY2025, 3.25x at 2026-03-31 and 2.83x at 2026-06-30, and negative 0.21x at 2026-09-30, while EBITDA (Reported) over cash interest is negative from FY2025. The issuer nevertheless reports interest coverage of 2.28x against a 2.00x minimum for the four quarters to 2026-09-30, so the covenant definition of adjusted earnings must differ materially from the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA; the filings do not print that definition, so no covenant headroom is inferred here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C-LA5; calculation C-LI5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that the third-quarter loss is more than accounted for by charges of about USD 671.6 million for pricing and rebate adjustments on inventory held by channel customers, which the cash flow statement adds back as non-cash. Before those charges, third-quarter adjusted EBITDA would have been USD 113.0 million and last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA USD 618.1 million, giving total debt over EBITDA of 6.76x, a normalisation that is an Analyst Judgement and not an issuer measure. That view would win if accrued customer rebates, which rose from USD 417.4 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 811.9 million at 2026-09-30, were settled by credit notes rather than cash; if they are paid in cash they exceed the USD 735.8 million of cash held, so the earnings loss converts into a cash call.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C-M1; calculation C-M2; calculation C-D9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 45–47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow was negative in both nine-month periods and the 2026 improvement came from sources that do not repeat. Net cash from operating activities was negative USD 285.5 million for nine months 2026 against negative USD 717.0 million for nine months 2025. The 2026 figure includes the USD 200.0 million prepayment from Corteva for rimisoxafen supply, recorded as deferred revenue, so without it operating cash flow would have been negative USD 485.5 million, and income taxes paid fell to USD 36.8 million from USD 156.3 million. A prepayment is an obligation to deliver product, not earned cash, so it supports liquidity without supporting debt service from earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C-O1; calculation C-O2; calculation C-O3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7, 14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Seasonal working capital is the other swing: advance payments from customers fell by USD 452.6 million in nine months 2026, almost the same as in nine months 2025, and the revolver was drawn to USD 1,109.5 million at 2026-03-31, leaving only USD 666.9 million available at that date. If the seasonal pattern repeats, the first quarter of 2027 would again draw heavily on the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is high against the earlier dates but was rebuilt with one-off sources. Cash was USD 735.8 million and revolver funds available USD 1,661.4 million at 2026-09-30, a total of USD 2,397.2 million against USD 1,057.8 million at 2026-03-31, the highest of the five balance-sheet dates shown. The rebuild came from USD 1,200.0 million of Senior Secured Notes due 2031 issued in June 2026, which redeemed the notes due October 2026 and repaid revolver borrowings, from USD 403.2 million of equity proceeds in September 2026 and from the licensing prepayment. Of the cash, USD 486.1 million is held by foreign subsidiaries; only USD 72.8 million of debt other than the revolver borrowing falls due within one year and the revolving credit facility commitment matures in 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C-LQ5; calculation C-LQ3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23, 69

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The refinancing risk has moved from the 2026 maturities to the covenant package and the secured structure: the leverage covenant is not applied for the first three quarters of 2026 and resumes at a maximum of 6.75x from the quarter ending 2026-12-31, while the new secured notes carry first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the company and its main guarantors. The filings state no security for the senior notes or the subordinated notes and do not state how the secured revolver ranks against the new secured notes, so the position of those notes in a recovery is not established here; the net proceeds of the India sale, which is pending regulatory approval, are directed by Amendment No. 8 to repaying the revolver or to general and working capital needs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier finance and customer-funded items carry more of working capital than the debt tables show. Obligations confirmed under the supply chain finance program were USD 213.1 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 109.5 million at 2025-12-31, an increase of USD 103.6 million that sits in trade payables and is paid out of operating cash flow; guarantees of vendor financing for customers were USD 51.6 million. Accrued customer rebates of USD 811.9 million exceed cash of USD 735.8 million. If suppliers stopped using the program or customers drew down rebates in cash, working capital would absorb cash that the revolver would have to fund.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C-S1; calculation C-D9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 41–42

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer advance payments are a seasonal float that ran from USD 453.1 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 67.8 million at 2026-09-30, and the licensing prepayment of USD 200.0 million sits in other long-term liabilities. Receivables sold under securitization programs, mainly in Brazil, were USD 134.4 million in nine months 2026 and are not in debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two events after 2026-09-30 are flagged and kept out of the period figures: the cash dividend of USD 12.6 million paid on 2026-10-15, which raises pro forma net debt to USD 3,454.5 million, and Amendment No. 8 to the credit agreement dated 2026-10-21, which requires the net proceeds of the India sale to repay revolver debt or fund general or working capital needs and conditionally releases some guarantors and collateral. The India sale for USD 252 million and the Newark, Delaware property sale were not complete at the report date, so neither is in net debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The India business appears with different figures in different roles: sale consideration of USD 252 million subject to adjustments, net assets held for sale of USD 282.6 million, a carrying value of USD 260.0 million after a USD 22.6 million translation gain, an impairment of USD 57.1 million in nine months 2026, and a USD 145.2 million India line in the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation. All are kept, each with its role, and none is chosen as the single India figure; the consideration is USD 30.6 million below net assets held for sale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C-R1; calculation C-R2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 21, 51

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main data risk is definitional: the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA differs from reported EBITDA by USD 2,508.9 million for the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, the covenant definition of adjusted earnings is not printed, and the India business is in adjusted EBITDA before Q3 2025 but out of it afterwards. Senior notes appear as one line in every debt note, so the instrument table and the maturity ladder after 2029 rest on aggregates, and only the Senior Secured Notes have a stated legal rank. Interim last-twelve-months figures are built from year-to-date stubs and the 2026-03-31 figure mixes India perimeters for one quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA is negative in every period after FY2024, so only the first row is measurable, and the adjusted-basis ratios stay in the calculation register.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA is the unadjusted measure, which carries restructuring, impairment and India held for sale charges, so the negative values are not an adjusted cover measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Of the cash at 2026-09-30, USD 486.1 million is held by foreign subsidiaries, so not all of it is freely available to repay debt at the parent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Maturities are contractual principal at 2026-09-30 and the split of the remaining senior notes by year is not printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Adjusted EBITDA is the issuer-adjusted measure in every row, and the 2026-09-30 value is negative because the third quarter alone was USD 558.6 million negative.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Subsequent events flagged: Amendment No. 8 to the credit agreement is dated 2026-10-21; a cash dividend was paid on 2026-10-15; the sale of the India commercial business and the sale of the Newark, Delaware property were not complete at the report date; the Tessenderlo Group share purchase completed in September 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Senior notes are printed as one aggregate line in every debt note (carrying value USD 1,998.7 million and principal USD 2,000.0 million at 2026-09-30, coupons 3.5% to 6.4%, maturities 2029 to 2053); the principal, coupon, maturity, obligor and guarantors of each series are not stated, so the instrument table carries the aggregate, the ladder after 2029 is one bucket, and instrument-level maturity and recovery work is restricted. Severity: High. Action: obtain the senior notes indenture supplements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant definitions of adjusted earnings and of the baskets are not printed, so the reported interest coverage of 2.28x and secured leverage of 1.37x for the four quarters to 2026-09-30 cannot be reconciled with adjusted EBITDA, which is negative for the last twelve months; covenant headroom cannot be assessed and none is inferred. Severity: High. Action: obtain the credit agreement and its amendments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The legal rank of the revolving credit facility, the senior notes, the subordinated notes, the pollution control bonds and the foreign debt is not stated, so only the Senior Secured Notes appear in the debt stack and no cumulative leverage is stated for any facility. Severity: High. Action: obtain the indentures and the intercreditor terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage at 2026-09-30 is not calculable on either EBITDA basis because last-twelve-months EBITDA is not above zero, and reported-basis leverage is not calculable at FY2025 and at 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30 for the same reason; the leverage chart and the calculation register show the gap, never zero. Severity: Medium. Action: recompute when the fourth quarter of 2026 is reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The maturity ladder at 2026-09-30 is derived because the quarterly report prints none: the 2029 senior notes amount of USD 500.0 million is carried from the 2025-12-31 ladder, and the rest after 2029 is one bucket. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain per-series maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 144; calculation C-P2; calculation C-P3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The size and limit of the supply chain finance program and the share of trade payables it represents are not stated; only the obligations confirmed as valid (USD 213.1 million at 2026-09-30) are printed. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the program terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The last-twelve-months figures at 2026-03-31 mix India perimeters because the current stub excludes India and the prior-year stub includes it, and Adjusted EBITDA before Q3 2025 includes India; the 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30 figures exclude India throughout. Severity: Low. Action: use the issuer's revenue excluding India for like-for-like growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - EBITDA (Reported) is calculated because the issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA; a lender or agency definition may differ. Severity: Low. Action: none beyond labelling the basis in every quotation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Statement cells shown as Not supplied are source dashes or lines a filing does not print for that period: goodwill at 2025-12-31, assets and liabilities held for sale at 2024-12-31, adjustments for commercial actions before nine months 2026, several financing lines in interim columns and fees associated with issuance of common stock before nine months 2026, and the free cash flow and revenue-excluding-India cells the issuer does not print for a period in the KPI dashboard; none is read as zero. Severity: Low. Action: none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - In the instrument table, security, ranking, rate type, reference rate, spread, floor and annual amortisation are Not supplied wherever the filings do not state them (the rate type of the notes, pollution control bonds and foreign debt within long-term debt, the reference rate, spread and floor of the revolver, and the security of the subordinated notes). The market risk disclosure states only that the variable-rate part of the debt, 5 percent at 2026-09-30, is principally the credit facility and foreign subsidiary credit lines. The entity names and entity-level figures of the subsidiary guarantors are not printed, and none of these items is inferred from an instrument name. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the indentures and the guarantor list.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash flows are printed year-to-date only, so discrete second-quarter and third-quarter cash flows and fourth-quarter 2025 cash flows are not stated; fourth-quarter 2025 Adjusted EBITDA is calculated as the fiscal year less nine months. Severity: Low. Action: none beyond labelling the derived quarters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The currency of short-term foreign debt and foreign debt within long-term debt is not stated, so no foreign exchange conversion is made; the filing prints their amounts in USD. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the foreign debt note detail.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fmc Corp (FMC Corporation, issuer id fmc-37785), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business, ownership, transactions, governance behaviour and operating model of the issuer, drawn from the five supplied filings. No fact dated after 2026-10-30 is used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: FMC is a listed agricultural chemicals producer whose creditors now depend on a new 20% strategic shareholder, pending asset sales and secured borrowing, because third-quarter 2026 gross margin was negative USD 401.6 million and the patents on its main diamide franchise have expired.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1A-1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In 2026 the company sold shares to Tessenderlo Group for USD 403.2 million, received a USD 200.0 million prepayment from Corteva under a supply and licence agreement, issued USD 1,200.0 million of secured notes and agreed to sell its India business for USD 252 million, each directed to debt reduction or liquidity. These steps buy time but do not repair earnings: third-quarter revenue was USD 105.9 million after about USD 672 million of pricing and rebate charges, and total equity is USD 9.5 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings name no sponsor and no controlling shareholder, so the usual sponsor-extraction risk is not evidenced, but a new holder of about 20% arrived in September 2026 on terms the filings do not describe. Tessenderlo Group bought shares issued from treasury at USD 13.30 each, and the proxy statement that would list other large holders and the board's independence is not supplied. Creditors cannot yet say whether this holder is a stabiliser with board or consent rights or a passive investor, because the investor agreement is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1A-1; calculation C1A-2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 186

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management has acted in creditors' favour on distributions and funding. The quarterly dividend fell from USD 0.58 to USD 0.08 per share, repurchases are barred until 2028-12-31, and the Tessenderlo equity, the Corteva prepayment and the secured notes proceeds went to repay the revolver and redeem notes. Cash dividends paid fell by 86.1% in the first nine months of 2026, which supports liquidity but does not restore earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims on assets now favour lien holders. The USD 1,200.0 million of notes due 2031 carry first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the company and its main guarantors, and the revolver is guaranteed and secured over certain assets and equity, partly released in June 2026. The filings do not state security for the existing senior and subordinated notes or how the liens rank against them, so the effect on those holders is not established here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is broad by region and product, but its revenue rests on a diamide franchise whose composition-of-matter patents have expired in every major market. The two diamide families produced about USD 1.2 billion, roughly 34.6% of FY2025 revenue, and 82.2% of the foreign granted diamide patents expire by the end of 2030, so generic price pressure is a continuing mechanism and not a one-time event.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1A-6; calculation C1A-11; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is concentrated by geography and input supply. Brazil and the United States together supplied 58.8% of FY2025 revenue, and critical intermediates come largely from outside the United States, principally China and India, so a regional channel shock or a trade disruption reaches earnings directly. The third quarter showed the channel mechanism: customers holding too much FMC inventory cut replenishment orders, and the company took about USD 672 million of pricing and rebate charges, of which USD 639 million reduced revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1A-5; calculation C1A-14; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The revenue base and the book equity cushion have both been sharply reduced. Third-quarter revenue fell 80.5% to USD 105.9 million, and total equity fell from USD 2,098.9 million to USD 9.5 million after the pricing charges, impairments and valuation allowances on deferred tax assets, which leaves almost no book equity beneath the debt. Recovery value therefore depends on asset sales and an earnings recovery, not on accounting capital.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1A-7; calculation C1A-9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two sales are the remaining named debt-reduction sources and both are conditional. The India commercial business is agreed at USD 252 million, subject to regulatory approvals and adjustments, and the property at the Newark, Delaware research headquarters is framed at about USD 114 million gross, subject to due diligence. Completed 2026 sources total USD 603.2 million and the pending sales would add USD 366 million gross.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1A-8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fmc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that outside capital arrived at the point of stress and the product pipeline is large. Tessenderlo Group paid USD 13.30 per share for about 20% of the company in September 2026, Corteva prepaid USD 200.0 million for rimisoxafen supply under a licence on a molecule whose ownership FMC keeps, and management reports 19 new active ingredients in development and four actives being commercialised, among them a herbicide mode of action that management calls the first new one in over three decades. If the two pending sales close, 2026 sources of cash outside operations would reach USD 969.2 million gross.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1A-8; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the investor agreement shows the new holder has committed to support the company, if the India and Newark proceeds repay debt as planned, or if the new actives start to replace diamide revenue. It would worsen if either sale slips, if channel customers keep destocking so that further pricing charges follow, or if the investor agreement gives the holder rights that limit the board's room to protect creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement that lists beneficial owners, directors and related-party dealings is not supplied, so the ownership conclusion cannot name any holder other than Tessenderlo Group or state the board's independence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The investor agreement and registration rights agreement with Tessenderlo Group are not supplied, so the conclusion that the new holder's influence is unknown cannot be narrowed to a stabilising or a controlling role.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - FY2025 and nine-month 2026 revenue mixes are distorted by about USD 422 million of India charges in FY2025 and about USD 639 million of pricing charges in 2026, so the mix conclusions describe reported revenue and not underlying demand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The diamide revenue figures are rounded management statements of about USD 0.8 billion and USD 0.4 billion, so the share of revenue exposed to generic competition is approximate to within a few percentage points.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer concentration and distributor terms are not disclosed in the filings, so the diversification conclusion rests on regional and product mix only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No document dated after 2026-10-30 is supplied, so the status of the India and Newark sales and any later change in the shareholder base are not established beyond that date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three transactions in 2026 repaired liquidity and two sales remain open. Tessenderlo Group bought 30,319,166 shares issued from treasury at USD 13.30 each, for cash proceeds of USD 403.2 million after announcing the agreement on 2026-06-30; the company paid USD 8.0 million of fees, used the proceeds to repay revolver borrowings and for general purposes, and called the investment the conclusion of the strategic review begun in February 2026. In June 2026 Corteva prepaid USD 200.0 million for rimisoxafen to be supplied by FMC under a co-exclusive supply and licence agreement, which the company records as deferred revenue and so as an obligation to deliver product.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1A-2; calculation C1A-3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fmc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The new debt is USD 1,200.0 million of senior secured notes due 2031, completed on 2026-06-05 and used to redeem USD 500 million of senior notes due 2026-10-01, repay revolver borrowings and meet general corporate needs. The notes are guaranteed by subsidiaries in the United States, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Canada and Singapore and secured by first-priority liens, and the covenants on the notes limit dividends and further indebtedness. The revolver was amended in December 2025, April 2026, June 2026 and, after the balance sheet date, on 2026-10-21, each time changing covenant levels, security or the use of sale proceeds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two sales remain open. The India commercial business is agreed for USD 252 million with Crystal Crop Protection Limited, subject to regulatory approvals and adjustments for cash, debt and working capital, with closing expected in 2026; its carrying value is USD 260.0 million, USD 8.0 million above the stated consideration before adjustments. The framework agreement for the Newark property, about USD 114 million gross with a leaseback, was expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 but the latest report says only that it is subject to due diligence. Events after 2026-09-30 are a dividend of USD 12.6 million paid on 2026-10-15 and the eighth revolver amendment, which requires net India proceeds to repay revolver debt or fund general or working capital needs and conditionally releases some guarantors and security; the dividend payment is not in September cash and the amendment is not in the terms reported at that date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The module status is ready with limitations: the five filings support the business, transaction and behaviour registers, and the proxy statement and the Tessenderlo agreements are absent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Sponsor / Governance Risk Level is Medium: supportive financial policy and an outside equity investor coexist with a lien-based refinancing, repeated covenant amendments and an unknown set of rights held by a new 20% shareholder.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The orchestrator selects the next module.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fmc Corp (FMC Corporation, issuer id fmc-37785), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the integrated fundamental credit view of the consolidated company, built from the five supplied filings and the three earlier module outputs. No fact dated after 2026-10-30 is used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Credit quality is weak and dependent on one-off funding: earnings cannot carry the debt, so creditors rely on liquidity of USD 2,397.2 million, covenant relief and pending asset sales, while noteholders with no stated security now rank behind new secured lenders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2-1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA was negative USD 53.5 million at 2026-09-30, so leverage cannot be measured. Before USD 671.6 million of third-quarter pricing charges it would have been USD 618.1 million, close to the USD 618.9 million that a 6.75x ceiling requires at the September debt level when the leverage test returns on 2026-12-31. The covenant definition of earnings is not printed, so headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2-8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings no longer carry the debt, and the damage is wider than one quarter's charges. Third-quarter 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was negative USD 558.6 million, and even before the pricing charges it would have been USD 113.0 million against USD 236.1 million a year earlier, a fall of 52.1%. Revenue excluding India and before the charges fell 16.2% over nine months, and gross margin was 10.81% of revenue against 35.73%. Price pressure on legacy products and lower volumes sit under the channel charges, so the earnings base to which leverage returns is lower than the FY2025 figure of USD 842.7 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2-9; calculation C2-10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is weak because the main franchise has lost patent protection and demand is being destocked. The two diamide product families supplied about 34.6% of FY2025 revenue, their composition-of-matter patents have expired in the major markets, and the company names generic producers, particularly in China, as a continuing pricing threat. Brazil and the United States supplied 58.8% of FY2025 revenue, customers are running very low inventory in response to high financing costs and demand uncertainty, and growers are buying carefully because of low crop prices and elevated input costs, so a regional destocking cycle reaches group earnings directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for the next year but was bought with funding that does not repeat. Cash of USD 735.8 million and revolver availability of USD 1,661.4 million total USD 2,397.2 million, equal to 3.89 times the first-quarter 2026 operating cash outflow of USD 616.6 million, or 3.10 times if the USD 486.1 million of cash held by foreign subsidiaries is excluded. Net debt was USD 3,441.9 million at 2026-09-30 and USD 3,454.5 million pro forma for the USD 12.6 million dividend paid on 2026-10-15; pro forma cash and pro forma net leverage are not established. Only USD 72.8 million of principal falls due within one year and the revolver matures in 2028, so the near-term risk is cash burn and the covenant package, not a maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2-1; calculation C2-2; calculation C2-3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow has almost no room even on the pre-charge earnings base. Interest, dividends, guided environmental and restructuring spending and capital expenditure total USD 606.2 million to USD 636.2 million in 2026, against pre-charge last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 618.1 million, before cash taxes and working capital. The company expects 2026 free cash flow to be slightly below FY2025's negative USD 165.3 million, which caps fourth-quarter 2026 free cash flow at USD 123.6 million against USD 623.2 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, and nine-month free cash flow was negative USD 488.9 million without the Corteva prepayment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2-4; calculation C2-5; calculation C2-19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 78–79

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The leverage test that returns on 2026-12-31 is the sharpest near-term risk and cannot be sized. The revolver covenant tests debt to adjusted earnings, not applied in the first three quarters of 2026, at a maximum of 6.75x through 2027-12-31, stepping down to 3.75x by the quarter ended March 31, 2029; interest cover must stay at 2.00x or more until June 30, 2027, rising to 3.50x by March 31, 2029. The company reports interest cover of 2.28x and secured leverage of 1.37x against a 3.50x maximum, yet its own Adjusted EBITDA over cash interest is negative 0.21x, so the covenant earnings definition must add back most of the third-quarter charges and the filings do not print it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2-8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Structure now favours lien holders, and holders with no stated security are the exposed group. The USD 1,200.0 million of 8.00% senior secured notes due 2031 carry first-priority liens on substantially all assets of the company and its main guarantors, and the revolver is secured over certain assets, so secured debt is 32.0% of principal and could reach 51.2% if the available revolver were drawn. The filings state no security for the USD 2,000.0 million of senior notes or the USD 750.0 million of subordinated notes, so those holders rank behind the collateral on the same assets, and the December 2025 amendment also provided for a lien over substantially all assets if two agencies rate the company below BB+ or Ba1, a trigger whose status the filings do not state.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2-14; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is supportive, but the equity cushion is thin and asset sales are conditional. The dividend was cut to USD 0.08 per share, repurchases are barred until 2028-12-31, and USD 603.2 million of equity and licence cash has been raised, with USD 366 million gross more pending from the India and Newark sales. Book equity is USD 9.5 million; at Tessenderlo's USD 13.30 purchase price, equity is worth USD 2,068.9 million, so debt is 66.9% of debt plus equity at that price, and the issuer estimates debt fair value at 90.4% of carrying value.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2-11; calculation C2-12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk is about price and priority, not near-term dates. Of USD 4,222.8 million of principal, 82.9% matures after 2029, and the two newest series carry coupons of 8.00% and 8.45%, while third-quarter interest expense rose 14.82% on the prior year. A holder of the 2029 senior notes of USD 500.0 million faces the first large maturity after the revolver, and the secured structure is likely to make refinancing harder for holders with no stated security.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2-6; calculation C2-13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside debt are large relative to cash and compete with debt service. Accrued customer rebates of USD 811.9 million exceed cash at 2026-09-30 by USD 76.1 million (pro forma cash for the October dividend is not established), environmental liabilities are USD 566.0 million with about USD 304 million more reasonably possible, and the Corteva prepayment of USD 200.0 million is owed in product. None of these is in the USD 4,177.7 million of debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weak view is that outside capital arrived at the point of stress and the pre-charge earnings base is still positive. Tessenderlo paid USD 13.30 per share for about 20% of the company, Corteva prepaid USD 200.0 million, the pre-charge Adjusted EBITDA of USD 618.1 million covers annualised third-quarter interest expense of USD 294.4 million 2.10 times, capital expenditure was cut 57.8% over nine months, and the Project Foundation restructuring targets USD 200 million of annual savings by the end of 2027. The issuer also reports covenant compliance at 2026-09-30 and a revolver of USD 2,000.0 million with a 2028 maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2-7; calculation C2-15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the fourth quarter shows no new pricing charges and channel inventory normalises, if the India and Newark proceeds repay debt, and if the credit agreement defines covenant earnings so that the 2026-12-31 leverage test is met with room. It would worsen if further pricing adjustments follow in North America, if accrued rebates are settled in cash, if the India sale slips beyond 2026, or if a further revolver amendment is needed at the first test date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement is not supplied, so the conclusion about the 2026-12-31 leverage test rests on arithmetic from the reported ratios and on a ceiling of 6.75x; a definition that adds back less than the third-quarter charges could produce a breach at the first test date, and one that adds back more would widen the cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The USD 671.6 million add-back that gives pre-charge earnings is an analyst normalisation, and the company says it also changed its North American pricing and rebate model, so part of the charge may recur and underlying earnings could be below USD 618.1 million, which would weaken the free cash flow and cover conclusions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer set or sector benchmark is supplied, so the business profile is judged in absolute terms and its standing against typical leveraged issuers is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The equity cushion uses the USD 13.30 price paid in September 2026, not a current share price, and the only debt market measure is the issuer's aggregate fair value, so the conclusion on market confidence could change with a dated quote for any series.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management guidance is directional only, so the fourth-quarter free cash flow cap is a derived bound and the cash conclusion is bounded rather than forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The lien ranking among the revolver, the secured notes and the senior and subordinated notes is not printed, so the structural priority conclusion identifies the exposed holders but does not size recovery.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit strength is liquidity and funding access in the near term: USD 2,397.2 million of cash and revolver availability, a revolver that runs to 2028, only USD 72.8 million of principal due within one year, and no maturity above USD 150.0 million before the USD 500.0 million senior notes in 2029. The mechanism is that equity, a licence prepayment and secured notes retired the 2026 maturity and repaid the revolver, which gives creditors time. The implication is that a payment default before 2028 would likely need a cash burn well above the 2026 pattern.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A second strength is cooperative financial policy. The dividend is down to USD 0.08 per share, repurchases are barred until 2028-12-31, new equity went to debt repayment, and capital expenditure was cut 57.8% over nine months. The implication is that cash is being kept for creditors; cash dividends paid fell by USD 188.0 million in nine months 2026, which is modest next to cash interest of USD 250.8 million over twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A third strength is cost action and optionality: Project Foundation targets USD 200 million of annual run-rate savings by the end of 2027 and the pipeline includes four new active ingredients, and pending sales add USD 366 million gross. These are conditional and arrive after cash costs, so they support the downside case only if delivered.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main weakness is the earnings collapse. Third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA was negative USD 558.6 million, the last twelve months are negative USD 53.5 million, and even pre-charge earnings fell 52.1% in the quarter. The mechanism is generic competition on the diamides and destocking by customers who face low crop prices, and the implication is that leverage cannot be sized and covenants, not earnings, set the pace.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is priority and structure: first-lien secured notes and a secured revolver put 32.0% of principal ahead of the holders of senior and subordinated notes, for which no security is stated, rising to 51.2% on a full revolver draw, with a rating-triggered lien provision and repeated amendments that release and add collateral. The third is thin capital: total equity of USD 9.5 million, claims outside debt in the form of rebates of USD 811.9 million, environmental liabilities of USD 566.0 million and supplier finance of USD 213.1 million, and free cash flow near zero after fixed cash claims. The fourth is concentration, in one patent-exposed franchise and in Brazil and the United States.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The reporting entity is FMC Corporation, consolidated with its subsidiaries; the filings describe no separate finance subsidiary and print no guarantor financial information, so debt, earnings, leverage and cover are read at the consolidated level, with the parent's own figures not separable. FMC is a global agricultural sciences company with one business segment, selling insecticides, herbicides and fungicides and a plant health line of biologicals, crop nutrition and seed treatment. FY2025 revenue was USD 3,467.4 million, down 18.3% from USD 4,246.1 million, with insecticides 45.4%, herbicides 36.0%, fungicides 10.5%, plant health 5.5% and other 2.7%, and Latin America 39.0%, North America 31.8%, Europe, Middle East and Africa 25.1% and Asia 4.1%. The business model supports cash-flow visibility only weakly: sales are seasonal, flow through distributors that are holding elevated FMC inventory and cutting replenishment, and are priced against generic suppliers, so debt service depends on the pricing cycle rather than on contracted revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is listed. No sponsor or controlling shareholder is named, and the only identified large holder is a new one; Tessenderlo Group NV bought 30,319,166 shares from treasury at USD 13.30, which is 19.49% of the 155,558,399 shares outstanding, under an Investor Agreement whose terms are not supplied, and the chief executive officer is also chairman. The supportive reading is that outside equity repaid debt and the strategic review ended without a change of control; the open risk is that an unknown set of nomination, consent or transfer rights sits with a holder of about 20%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue drivers are volume, price and channel inventory. Price is the more important: the third-quarter report states that pricing pressure continued primarily on core legacy products and that growers are buying carefully because of low crop prices and high input costs. Pass-through is limited because the company granted price adjustments on inventory already held by channel customers, which converts a price cut into a charge against revenue. The credit implication is that revenue may not recover to FY2025 levels when destocking ends, because the price level, not only the volume, has reset.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are not defended under volume and price pressure. Gross margin fell from 37.0% of revenue in FY2025 to 10.81% in nine months 2026, selling, general and administrative expense rose 3.9% while revenue fell 27.4%, and research and development was 7.7% of FY2025 revenue and USD 183.6 million in nine months 2026. Fixed overhead and research spending therefore deleverage quickly. Management levers exist: Project Foundation exits high-cost plants with a targeted USD 200 million of annual savings by the end of 2027, at a cost of USD 700 million to USD 775 million of total pre-tax charges, of which USD 490 million to USD 505 million is non-cash. Business & governance reported the savings target as not supplied; the third-quarter 2026 report prints it, and this answer corrects that point.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 79; calculation C2-16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Input costs and supply carry trade risk: critical intermediates come largely from China and India, and the annual report cites tariffs and trade uncertainty as raising the cost of goods. Capital intensity is low, with capital expenditure of USD 96.3 million in FY2025, USD 29.7 million in nine months 2026 and USD 45 million to USD 55 million guided for 2026, so capex flexibility is already used. Restructuring cash of about USD 180 million, environmental spending of USD 80 million to USD 100 million, cash interest of USD 250.8 million over twelve months and dividends of about USD 50.4 million a year absorb the earnings that remain, which is why free cash flow converts at close to zero.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2-19; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 78–79

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry and substitutes are the dominant forces. Generic producers, mainly Chinese, compete on the same active ingredients as patents expire, competitors have consolidated into larger groups, and seed-applied technologies are alternatives. The mechanism is price: generic entry lowers the price at which FMC can hold volume, which cuts margin on the diamide franchise of about 34.6% of revenue. Buyer power is high because distributors and co-operatives hold the inventory and can defer orders, and the channel charges show it. Supplier power is moderate: critical intermediates from China and India expose cost and continuity to tariffs and trade measures, and take-or-pay purchase obligations of USD 179.9 million at 2025-12-31 fix part of the cost. New entrants matter mainly as generic registrants, and formulation, mixture and data protection still run longer than the expired composition-of-matter patents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_fmc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: External factors matter for credit only through four channels: trade measures and tariffs on intermediates, the Brazilian real and other currency exposure on a revenue base that is 32.2% Brazilian, crop prices and grower margins, and environmental regulation, where USD 566.0 million of liabilities and about USD 304 million of further reasonably possible loss compete with debt service. The Portland Harbor site added about USD 20 million to the reserve in the third quarter, with a further USD 31 million considered reasonably possible.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the issuer needs three things: no further channel charges, closing of the India and Newark sales, and a leverage covenant definition that works at 2026-12-31. Tailwinds are lower cash taxes, the working-capital release in the seasonally strong fourth quarter, capex of USD 45 million to USD 55 million and the Project Foundation savings; headwinds are generic diamide competition, restructuring and environmental cash, the 8.00% and 8.45% coupons and weak grower economics. Over three to five years the credit rests on whether new active ingredients (Isoflex, fluindapyr, Dodhylex and rimisoxafen) replace diamide revenue before the 2029 and 2031 maturities. Events after the balance sheet date are a dividend of USD 12.6 million paid on 2026-10-15 and Amendment No. 8 of 2026-10-21, which requires net India proceeds to repay the revolver or fund general or working capital needs and conditionally releases some guarantors and security; neither is in the September figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside scenario is a second round of channel adjustments. Initiating condition: customers keep destocking and the North American pricing reset does not hold. First operational break: fourth-quarter 2026 orders stay near the third-quarter level and a further pricing charge is booked. Financial transmission: accrued rebates of USD 811.9 million are settled in cash rather than credit notes and the fourth-quarter working-capital inflow stays below the USD 123.6 million cap, leaving 2026 free cash flow worse than FY2025. Liquidity and leverage consequence: the 2026-12-31 leverage test applies with covenant earnings that may not reach USD 618.9 million, and the first-quarter 2027 seasonal outflow, USD 616.6 million in the first quarter of 2026, draws on liquidity of USD 2,397.2 million that excludes any India proceeds. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 if the revolver stays available, but availability depends on the covenant, so a covenant amendment, a further collateral grant or closing of the sales would be the likely route; management levers are those sales, capex, dividend of USD 12.6 million a quarter and restructuring. The observable triggers are a new revenue charge, a revolver amendment, and the India sale slipping past 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2-3; calculation C2-4; calculation C2-8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_fmc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, FMC presents an adequate but deteriorating business profile supported by a broad product and regional range, an extensive pipeline and a restructuring programme, but credit quality is constrained by collapsed earnings, a patent-exposed franchise, thin book equity and a secured structure that ranks lien holders first. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow is near zero at the pre-charge earnings base. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the India and Newark sales, the covenant definition and a recovery in pricing before the 2029 and 2031 maturities. The primary downside path is a second round of channel charges that turns the 2026-12-31 leverage test into an amendment request and draws on the revolver. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and indentures, the Tessenderlo Investor Agreement, rating levels, dated bond quotes and a peer set; the business profile against typical leveraged issuers is not established because no peer set is supplied. Credit synthesis completed. Top risk: covenant and liquidity dependence on earnings that are currently negative.
